articles.title: Gandhi Sagar Hosts Destination Cabinet Meeting Focused on Comprehensive Development of State and Mandsaur Region
articles.summary: Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav chaired the ninth Destination Cabinet meeting at Gandhi Sagar Forest Retreat in Gandhi Sagar in Mandsaur district. Chief Minister Dr. Yadav said, briefing the media on the Cabinet decisions, that the Cabinet had taken several far-reaching decisions on integrated industrial development, investment promotion, renewable energy, air connectivity, and administrative reforms in Madhya Pradesh. To expand industrial infrastructure, the Cabinet approved the establishment of an Agro Park over 178.83 hectares at Basai village and a dedicated Chemical Park over more than 3,500 acres at Kurlasi village in Mandsaur district; a Bio-Pharma Park over 1,121 acres in Ratlam; and a Textile and Allied Industries Park over 842.88 acres at Bhainsola in Dhar district. The Cabinet also approved the development of a Deep-Tech Research and Innovation Park in Ujjain with a grant of ₹237 crore and the participation of IIT Indore, the second phase of the Telecom Manufacturing Zone over 182.289 hectares in Gwalior, and the establishment of an industrial area in place of the proposed SEZ at Sausar in Pandhurna district. To encourage investment, the Cabinet approved amendments to the Madhya Pradesh Industrial Promotion Policy, 2025, along with the Policy Framework-2026. These amendments will broaden the definition of mega industrial units and extend eligibility to independent research and development units and centres of excellence. To strengthen the MSME and start-up ecosystem, the Cabinet approved the formation of a new government company, MP MSME Limited, with an initial paid-up capital of ₹10 crore and a budgetary provision of ₹11 crore. It also approved the appointment of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) as the national partner of MPIDC and MPSEDC for investment promotion activities. In a significant and long-awaited decision concerning government employees, the Cabinet approved the removal of the provision and the related clarification concerning ‘more than two living children’ from the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services Rules. It also decided to terminate, with immediate effect, all pending disciplinary proceedings initiated on this basis. To promote clean energy and air connectivity, the Cabinet approved a 200 MW floating solar project at the Omkareshwar Reservoir, along with a battery energy storage system with a minimum capacity of 800 MWh under Phase II. The Cabinet also approved amendments to the Madhya Pradesh Civil Aviation Policy, 2025, extending the period of Viability Gap Funding (VGF) assistance for new air routes from one year to four years for domestic routes and two years for international routes. The Cabinet also took an important decision to expedite the disposal of cases under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act. It approved 72 posts, including those of judges and senior public prosecutors, for establishing six special courts in Indore, Mandsaur, Neemuch, Singrauli, Bhopal and Rewa. Agro Park Approved at Basai Village in Mandsaur The Cabinet approved the establishment of the Agro Park Mandsaur over 178.83 hectares at Basai village in the western Malwa region, along with a special financial assistance package for industrial units to be established there. It also approved the constitution of a special committee to oversee the allotment of land to industrial units in the proposed industrial area. The Secretary in charge of the Department of Industrial Policy and Investment Promotion, whether Additional Chief Secretary, Principal Secretary or Secretary, will head the committee. Its members will include the Managing Director of MPIDC, Bhopal; Executive Director, MPIDC Regional Office, Ujjain; Executive Director (Land Management), MPIDC; and Chief Engineer, MPIDC. Industrial units belonging to three major sectors and their associated activities will be eligible for land allotment in the Agro Park. The first sector will cover agriculture and food processing, including processing of garlic, onion, coriander, cumin, fenugreek and soybean; spice oleoresin and essential oil extraction; dehydration plants; orange pulp and juice processing; and cold-chain facilities. The second sector will cover Ayush and herbal products, including phytochemicals, nutraceuticals, Ayurvedic medicines and pharmaceutical derivatives based on medicinal crops such as Ashwagandha, Isabgol, Tulsi and Chia. The third sector will comprise agricultural and food-related engineering and packaging. It will include units manufacturing high-precision agricultural processing equipment, micro-irrigation equipment such as drip and sprinkler systems, food-processing machinery and food-grade packaging materials. Industrial units established in the Agro Park will receive additional incentives over and above those available under the existing Industrial Promotion Policy, 2025. Under land-related assistance, units will receive an additional 25 per cent concession on the prevailing land premium rate. Land development charges, ground rent (calculated at the applicable rate before the additional concession) and other charges will be levied as per the prevailing land allotment rules. Under the electricity assistance provision, eligible units will receive a tariff concession of ₹2 per unit (kWh) for seven years from the commencement of commercial production. The amount will be reimbursed to the units by MPIDC. For water supply, units will be provided water at a fixed rate of ₹25 per kilolitre for five years. The special financial assistance package for large industrial units will be governed by the provisions of the Industrial Promotion Policy, 2025, and the Madhya Pradesh Investment Promotion Scheme, 2025. Similarly, MSME units will be covered under the Madhya Pradesh MSME Development Policy, 2025, and the Madhya Pradesh MSME Promotion Scheme, 2025. Projects associated with other departments will be governed by the respective departmental policies and rules. The Agro Park is expected to involve an expenditure of approximately ₹85 crore over three years. Around 47 industrial units, comprising MSMEs and large-scale enterprises, are likely to be established there. These units are expected to attract investments of approximately ₹3,200 crore and generate employment for more than 14,000 people. Chemical Park Approved at Kurlasi Village in Mandsaur The Cabinet approved sending a proposal to the Government of India for establishing a dedicated Chemical Park over more than 3,500 acres at Kurlasi village in Garoth Tehsil of Mandsaur district under the Central Government's 'BHAVYA – Scheme for Chemical Parks'. MPIDC has been appointed as the nodal and implementing agency for submitting the proposal to the Government of India. In-principle approval has also been granted for a minimum contribution of ₹500 crore by the State Government towards developing basic infrastructure and common utilities for the park. In addition, MPIDC Limited has been authorised to undertake the necessary proceedings before the Madhya Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission for obtaining an electricity distribution licence. Eligible industrial units established in the Kurlasi Chemical Park will receive special incentives over and above those available under the prevailing Industrial Promotion Policy, 2025. These include electricity at ₹5 per unit for the initial 10 years and industrial water at ₹25 per kilolitre for the same period. Eligible units will also receive reimbursement of stamp duty and registration charges, along with a state policy-based incentive package for 10 years. The Central Government will provide grant assistance of up to ₹1,000 crore for each park towards common infrastructure facilities and basic utilities. These will include wastewater treatment, waste management, water and steam systems, storage tank farms, solvent recovery, electricity distribution, firefighting and emergency response systems, and testing laboratories. The State Government will contribute a minimum of ₹500 crore towards common infrastructure and basic utilities. Approximately 150 industrial units, comprising MSMEs and large-scale enterprises, are expected to be established in the park. These units are likely to attract investments of around ₹15,000 crore and generate direct and indirect employment for approximately one lakh people. Bio-Pharma Park Approved in Ratlam Investment Region In an important step towards making Madhya Pradesh a national hub for biomanufacturing, the Cabinet approved the establishment of the 'Ratlam Bio-Pharma Park (Bioeconomy and Biomanufacturing Cluster)' over 1,121 acres in the Ratlam Investment Region. MPIDC has been appointed as the nodal agency for implementing the project. Eligible industrial units established in the park will receive special incentives over and above those available under the prevailing Industrial Promotion Policy, 2025. Land will be allotted at a token premium of ₹1 per square metre. Under the electricity tariff assistance provision, power will be made available at an effective rate of ₹5 per unit for seven years from the commencement of commercial production. MPIDC has been authorised to obtain a separate distribution licence for this purpose. Industrial water will also be supplied to the units at ₹25 per kilolitre for the initial seven years. The concerned department has been authorised to submit proposals under the Government of India's 'BioPharma Shakti Initiative' and other Central Government schemes for developing a Common Facility Centre in the park. It has also been clarified that units will not be eligible for duplicate assistance of the same nature. Applications for allotment of land, plots or buildings in the industrial area will be invited online. Allotments will be made after a comprehensive assessment of the investor's capacity, investment quantum, employment generation potential, technical capabilities, and land requirements in relation to availability. The Cabinet also approved the constitution of a special committee for this purpose. The Additional Chief Secretary of the Department of Industrial Policy and Investment Promotion will head the committee. Its members will include the Managing Director of MPIDC, Executive Director of MPIDC Regional Office, Ujjain, Executive Director (Land Management), MPIDC, and Chief Engineer, MPIDC. The Ratlam Bio-Pharma Park aims to develop the country's largest bioeconomy and biomanufacturing cluster in the Ratlam Investment Region. An expenditure of approximately ₹1,042 crore is envisaged over three years for its development. The park will accommodate units manufacturing biologics, biosimilars, vaccines, industrial and therapeutic enzymes, fermentation media (peptone and yeast extract), fermentation-based APIs/KSMs, vitamins and nutraceutical intermediates, precision fermentation products, and CDMO/CRO facilities. Around 150 industrial units are expected to be established, attracting investments of approximately ₹18,000 crore and generating around 25,000 jobs. Textile and Allied Industries Park Approved at Bhainsola in Dhar The Cabinet approved the establishment of the 'Textile and Allied Industries Park, Dhar' in the Bhainsola industrial area of Badnawar Tehsil, Dhar district. The dedicated industrial park will be developed on 842.88 acres (approximately 341.10 hectares) of land owned by MPIDC, adjoining the PM MITRA Park, Dhar. MPIDC will undertake its development, operation and maintenance. The corporation has also been authorised to initiate the necessary proceedings before the Madhya Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission for extending the scope of its electricity distribution licence to the park, as required in the future. Industrial units established in the Textile Park will receive special concessions and facilities over and above those available under the prevailing Madhya Pradesh Industrial Promotion Policy. Land will be allotted at a token price of ₹1 per square metre. Making optimum use of the investments made in PM MITRA Park, Dhar and the State Government will extend equivalent land, electricity and water facilities to units in the new park. Accordingly, electricity will be supplied at the same rates applicable to PM MITRA Park, Dhar, currently approximately ₹4.50 per unit, while water will be available at ₹25 per kilolitre. The provisions and conditions of the prevailing Madhya Pradesh Industrial Promotion Policy and the schemes issued under it will govern assistance to industrial units under this special financial assistance package. Land allotment in the park will be restricted exclusively to units engaged in textiles and allied activities. These will include spinning, weaving, knitting, processing (dyeing, printing and finishing), garment and apparel manufacturing, made-ups and home textiles, technical textiles, man-made fibre (MMF) and yarn, textile machinery and components, trims and accessories, and textile-related packaging, warehousing and logistics units. Interested units will be required to submit online applications for land allotment. Allotments will be made after assessing the investor's capacity, investment quantum, employment generation potential, land requirements and availability. A special committee will oversee the process. The Additional Chief Secretary or Principal Secretary of the Department of Industrial Policy and Investment Promotion, Madhya Pradesh Government, will head the committee. Its members will include the Managing Director of MPIDC, Bhopal; Executive Director of MPIDC Regional Office, Indore; Executive Director (Land Management), MPIDC; and Chief Engineer, MPIDC. An expenditure of approximately ₹835.50 crore is envisaged over three years for developing the Textile Park. Around 50 industrial units, comprising MSMEs and large-scale enterprises, are expected to be established. These units are likely to attract investments of approximately ₹6,150 crore and generate direct employment for around 35,000 people. Decision to Remove 'More Than Two Living Children' Provision for Government Employees The Cabinet approved the removal of Sub-rule (6) of Rule 6 of the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (General Conditions of Service) Rules, 1961. It also approved the deletion of the clarification concerning 'more than two living children' mentioned in Sub-rule (4) of Rule 22 of the Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1965. As per the Cabinet decision, all ongoing disciplinary proceedings against government employees solely on the ground of having more than two living children will be terminated with immediate effect. It has also been decided that cases in which competent authorities have already passed final orders imposing penalties through disciplinary proceedings on this ground will not be reopened. Amendments to Industrial Promotion Policy to Boost Investment and Employment The Cabinet approved significant amendments to the Madhya Pradesh Industrial Promotion Policy, 2025. The decision provides for expanding the definition and eligibility criteria of mega industrial units, revising the definitions and incentive provisions for the agriculture, dairy and food-processing sectors, and extending policy benefits to independent research and development units, testing laboratories and centres of excellence. The Department of Industrial Policy and Investment Promotion has been authorised to issue the necessary guidelines for implementing the revised provisions and make corresponding amendments to the Madhya Pradesh Investment Promotion Scheme, 2025. Under the approved amendments, the definition of a 'Mega-Scale Industrial Unit' under Clause 7.2 of the Industrial Promotion Policy, 2025, has been expanded. An industrial unit proposing or providing direct employment to 500 persons and investing ₹300 crore in plant and machinery will now qualify as a mega unit. In the general manufacturing sector, units investing ₹500 crore in plant and machinery will also qualify for this status. For large-scale industrial units established in priority development blocks and units in high-potential sectors, an investment of ₹250 crore in plant and machinery will qualify for mega-unit status. These high-potential sectors include personal care and cosmetics, petrochemicals, plastics and polymers, pharmaceuticals and biotechnology, renewable energy equipment manufacturing, and sunrise sectors notified by the State Government. For sectors such as agriculture, dairy and food processing, furniture manufacturing, garments and apparel, footwear, toys and accessories, gems and jewellery, herbal products and minor forest produce, and high-value-added manufacturing, an investment of ₹75 crore in plant and machinery will qualify a unit for mega status. These amendments will apply to all eligible applications under the policy. However, units that commenced commercial production one year before the date of issuance of the government order will not be eligible for benefits or reconsideration under the revised provisions. Clause 8.2.2 of the policy has also been amended to extend eligibility for assistance to independent research and development facilities, industrial testing and certification laboratories, and R&D units and centres of excellence holding national or international recognition, laboratory accreditation or sectoral regulatory approval from reputed institutions. These units will be eligible to undertake activities such as research, product development, prototyping, testing, technology transfer, commercialisation, industry-academia collaboration and incubation under a time-bound action plan. The definition of 'Agriculture, Dairy and Food Processing' has also been revised to include the processing of raw products obtained from agriculture, horticulture, dairy, fisheries, poultry and minor forest produce. The processing must involve changes in the basic physical properties of the product through the use of labour, electricity, machinery or capital, making the processed product suitable for human or animal consumption. The remaining provisions under this clause, namely Points 2 and 3, will remain unchanged. New provisions have also been added to Clauses 8.1 and 9.1.2. Accordingly, the first three large-scale agricultural and food-processing units established in any priority development block will be eligible for an additional geographical multiplier of 1.3. This provision will apply to units commencing production after the date of issuance of the relevant government order. Second Phase of Telecom Manufacturing Zone Approved in Gwalior The Cabinet approved the establishment of Phase II of the Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ), Gwalior. In-principle approval has been granted for setting up the second phase over a total area of 182.289 hectares (approximately 450.45 acres) in Talpura village (74.263 hectares) and Kulaith village (108.026 hectares) under the Special Area Development Authority (SADA), Gwalior. As part of the land-transfer process, the Urban Development and Housing Department or SADA will surrender the land to the Revenue Department under Clause 18 of the Madhya Pradesh Nazul Land Disposal Guidelines, 2020. The Revenue Department will subsequently transfer the land free of cost to the Department of Industrial Policy and Investment Promotion for TMZ Phase II. The Town and Country Planning Department will also initiate the process of changing the land use from residential to industrial under the Gwalior Development Plan-2035. The Cabinet authorised the Department of Industrial Policy and Investment Promotion and the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) to submit a proposal to the Government of India, Department of Telecommunications, seeking an additional grant of ₹500 crore for developing infrastructure in Phase II. The Cabinet also ratified the decision taken by the SPV's Board of Directors on October 13, 2026. Accordingly, the State Government's obligations under the MoU signed with the Department of Telecommunications for Phase I will also apply to Phase II. The special policy package and utility rates approved for the Telecom Manufacturing Zone will likewise be extended to industrial units in Phase II. MP MSME Limited Approved to Strengthen MSME and Start-up Ecosystem The Cabinet approved the formation of a new government company, 'MP MSME Limited', wholly owned by the State Government under the Companies Act, 2013, to strengthen Madhya Pradesh's micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and start-up ecosystem. The Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association of the proposed company were also approved. The Cabinet sanctioned an initial paid-up capital of ₹10 crore, along with the authorised share capital and initial financial provisions for the new company. It also approved the creation of a new budget head under Demand No. 35 (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises), with an initial budgetary provision and allocation of ₹11 crore for the company's establishment and subsequent operations. MP MSME Limited has been authorised to function as the principal implementing agency. The company will ensure effective implementation of the prevailing Madhya Pradesh MSME Industrial Land and Building Allotment and Management Rules, the Madhya Pradesh Start-up Policy and Implementation Plan, the Central Government's MSME policy, and all Central and State Government policies, packages and programmes related to the start-up sector. The Cabinet also approved the principal functions and responsibilities of the proposed company. The concerned administrative department has been authorised to complete the incorporation and other legal formalities. A separate proposal will be submitted by the administrative department regarding the human resource requirements for the company's administrative and organisational structure after its formation. The Chief Minister has also been authorised to make necessary changes to the company's Board of Directors. Following the revised classification of MSMEs and the evolving start-up ecosystem, the scope of the Madhya Pradesh MSME Development Policy, 2025, the Industrial Land and Building Allotment and Management Rules, 2025, and the Start-up Policy and Implementation Plan, 2025, has expanded considerably. Several activities are currently being implemented through different departmental offices and institutions. The new company is being established as a dedicated professional organisation to ensure effective coordination, professional management, investment promotion, time-bound implementation of schemes and development of industrial infrastructure. Deep-Tech Research and Innovation Park Approved in Ujjain The Cabinet took an important decision regarding the development, operation and management of the Deep-Tech Research and Innovation Park in Ujjain. A Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) will be constituted under the chairmanship of the Chief Minister. The Madhya Pradesh Council of Science and Technology (MPCST) will hold a 70 per cent stake, while MPIDC will hold the remaining 30 per cent. IIT Indore and other industrial partners will participate in the project, with IIT Indore serving as the principal academic and research partner for the park. Under the financial and land-related arrangements, the State Government's contribution of ₹237 crore will be transferred or reappropriated to MPCST in accordance with the applicable rules. This amount will be utilised as MPCST's contribution to the SPV. MPIDC will provide approximately 100 acres of land as its contribution to the SPV, and the park will be notified as an industrial area. Under this arrangement, the Department of Science and Technology, through MPCST, will serve as the majority sponsor and principal scientific institution. Its key responsibilities will include utilising the ₹237 crore grant, determining the park's scientific mission and programme priorities, leading collaborations with scientific and research institutions, and undertaking research and academic activities in partnership with IIT Indore. The Department of Industrial Policy and Investment Promotion, through MPIDC, will function as the land provider and nodal infrastructure facilitation agency. MPIDC will be responsible for notifying the park as an industrial area, facilitating licences and statutory approvals as the nodal agency under the EoDB Act, 2026, and supporting industrial outreach, land allotment and investor facilitation. As per the Cabinet decision, the SPV will have the authority to allot and lease land within the park in accordance with the approved rules and prevailing laws. The administrative department has been authorised to finalise the SPV's Memorandum of Association, Articles of Association, shareholders' agreement, and land allotment and lease rules in consultation with the Finance and Law Departments. Under the approved Board structure, the Chief Minister will serve as Chairman and the Chief Secretary as Vice-Chairman of the SPV. The Director General of MPCST will be its Managing Director. The Managing Director will be selected or nominated by the Chairman of the Board. The Board will include the Secretaries in charge of the Departments of Industrial Policy and Investment Promotion, Science and Technology, and Technical Education, Skill Development and Employment; the Managing Director of MPIDC; a representative of IIT Indore; and a representative of a scientific institution of national importance. Other members or representatives from the scientific and industrial communities may also be invited as special invitees, as required. Industrial Area Approved at Sausar in Pandhurna in Place of SEZ The Cabinet approved the establishment of an industrial area in place of the proposed Multi-Product Special Economic Zone (SEZ) by M/s Chhindwara Plus Developers Limited, Nagpur, in Sausar Tehsil of Pandhurna district. Accordingly, approval has been granted to change the designated purpose of government land allotted by the Revenue Department, along with acquired private land, from an SEZ to an industrial area. At the company's request, the lease period for the government land allotted to it has also been extended from 30 years to 99 years. As per the Cabinet decision, the rights granted to the company under Clause 4.9 of the Revenue Department's permission order dated March 20, 2013, will be transferred in favour of the company. These rights relate to the sale, mortgage, donation, leasing or other transfer of the allotted land, any part thereof, or any construction or building developed on it, which were earlier vested with the Revenue Department and the State Government. The company will also be required to deposit the applicable land premium and ground rent for the government land, along with the amounts equivalent to the stamp duty, registration charges and stamp duty concessions granted for establishing the SEZ, as calculated by the respective departments. Under the decision, 12.837 hectares of government land acquired under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, will be surrendered by the company and transferred to the Department of Industrial Policy and Investment Promotion. In addition, instead of taking 3.5 per cent sweat equity in the proposed SEZ project, the State Government will receive 3.5 per cent of the company's purchased private land, acquired private land and allotted government land. After the transfer of 12.837 hectares of government land to the department, the company will retain 1,175.55 hectares out of the total 1,188.387 hectares. Accordingly, 3.5 per cent of the remaining land, amounting to approximately 41.144 hectares, will be transferred by the company to the Department of Industrial Policy and Investment Promotion. ₹1,507 Crore Approved for MSME Infrastructure Development Scheme The Cabinet approved ₹1,507 crore for implementing the Infrastructure Development Scheme for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises under the Department of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises for the financial years 2026-27 to 2030-31. 200 MW Floating Solar Project with 800 MWh Battery Storage Approved at Omkareshwar The Cabinet approved a 200 MW floating solar project with an 800 MWh battery energy storage system under Phase II of the Omkareshwar Reservoir project. The initiative aims to ensure electricity supply during peak demand hours. The project will be connected to the Inter-State Transmission System. Following approval from the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, the bidding process through open tender will be coordinated by the Bid Process Coordinator. After commissioning the 200 MW capacity under Phase II, the combined capacity of Phase I (278 MW) and Phase II (200 MW) at the Omkareshwar Reservoir will reach 478 MW. This could make the Omkareshwar Floating Solar Project the world's largest floating solar project located on a single reservoir. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, Government of India, has announced the establishment of floating solar projects with a total capacity of 5,000 MW under the Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana, along with co-located energy storage systems providing a minimum of two hours of storage. The scheme provides for Central Financial Assistance of ₹1 crore per MW to reduce tariffs. According to the National Institute of Solar Energy's report, 'Solar PV Potential of India, June 2026', under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, the country's total floating solar potential stands at 102.18 GW. Of this, Madhya Pradesh accounts for 14.89 GW, approximately 15 per cent of the national potential. The first phase of the Omkareshwar Floating Solar Park, with a capacity of 278 MW, has been completed. It is India's largest operational floating solar project and among the largest operational projects of its kind in the world. Developed by Rewa Ultra Mega Solar Limited at a competitive tariff of ₹3.21 per kilowatt-hour, the electricity generated by this project has been procured by Madhya Pradesh Power Management Company Limited since 2024. CII Approved as National Partner of MPIDC and MPSEDC for Investment Promotion The Cabinet approved the appointment of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) as the national partner of MPIDC for three years to facilitate investment promotion activities in Madhya Pradesh under the Department of Industrial Policy and Investment Promotion. Under the national partnership agreement, CII will be reimbursed for the actual expenditure incurred on the assigned activities and responsibilities. No administrative charges or fees will be payable. The Managing Director of Madhya Pradesh Industrial Development Corporation Limited, Bhopal, has been authorised to complete all necessary formalities in this regard. The Cabinet also decided to appoint CII as the national partner of Madhya Pradesh State Electronics Development Corporation Limited (MPSEDC), an undertaking under the Department of Science and Technology. A separate agreement will be executed with CII by the concerned department. The Managing Director of MPSEDC has been authorised to complete all necessary formalities related to this arrangement. 72 Posts Approved for 6 Exclusive NDPS Special Courts The Cabinet approved 72 posts for establishing exclusive special courts in six districts—Indore, Mandsaur, Neemuch, Singrauli, Bhopal and Rewa—to ensure speedy trials of offences punishable under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (NDPS Act). As per the Cabinet decision, six posts of judges have been sanctioned for operating these special courts. In addition, six posts of senior public prosecutors have been approved to handle prosecution proceedings before these courts. A total of 72 posts have been sanctioned, including those for judges, senior public prosecutors and supporting staff. Ujjain Forest Zoo and Rescue Centre Approved at Naulakhi The Cabinet granted in-principle approval to a new scheme for establishing the Ujjain Forest Zoo and Rescue Centre over approximately 210 hectares at Naulakhi in Ujjain. The project aims to promote wildlife conservation, provide wildlife rescue and rehabilitation facilities for western Madhya Pradesh, strengthen conservation education and boost tourism in Ujjain. Madhya Pradesh Private Universities (Establishment and Operation) Amendment Bill, 2026 The Cabinet approved the necessary proceedings for introducing and passing the Madhya Pradesh Private Universities (Establishment and Operation) Amendment Bill, 2026, in the Legislative Assembly. The Bill relates to the establishment of Shri Radhe University in Morena. Amendments to Madhya Pradesh Civil Aviation Policy-2025 Approved The Cabinet approved amendments to the Madhya Pradesh Civil Aviation Policy, 2025, to expand air connectivity across the state. Under the revised provisions, the total period of Viability Gap Funding (VGF) assistance for introducing new destinations has been extended from one year to four years for domestic air routes and two years for international routes, commencing from the date of launch of the air service. Institutions already operating air services under the policy, whose initial one-year VGF assistance period is coming to an end, will be required to submit an application if they wish to continue their services. Such operators will be eligible for VGF assistance during the second year, amounting to 75 per cent of the assistance provided in the first year. At present, the policy provides VGF assistance for only one year for introducing new air destinations. Since a period of one year is considered insufficient for establishing a new air route, the Cabinet approved the extension of the assistance period to encourage the introduction and continuation of new air services. ₹414.17 Crore Approved for Shyam Shah Medical College, Rewa The Cabinet has granted administrative approval of ₹414.17 crore for the development of medical facilities at Shyam Shah Medical College in Rewa. The approved works include construction of an OPD block, maternity block, staff quarters and nursing college, along with the provision of biomedical equipment and hospital furniture. The project will also include other construction works and internal and external development works.

‘Symbol of indomitable courage, strong leadership’: Congress salutes Indira Gandhi on birth anniversary
articles.summary: New Delhi: Indira Gandhi was a revolutionary and continued to be one in government, making big decisions with fervour, love and commitment to her country, says Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra in a video shared by her mother Sonia Gandhi on former prime minister's birth anniversary on Thursday. Congress Parliamentary Chairperson Sonia Gandhi also recalled her first meeting with Indira Gandhi. In a post on X, Sonia Gandhi said, "The first time I was to meet Indira Gandhi, I refused to go. The next day I changed my mind. I was terribly nervous, and my English was poor, so she spoke to me in French. That was the first thing I learnt about her: she noticed what you were struggling with and quietly made it easier. "The world knew the Prime Minister. At home we knew Dadi -- a loving and gentle person, full of stories and wisdom and an incredible sense of humour," she said of her mother-in-law. "Some of her lives on in all of us, whether we know it or not. We still miss her," Sonia Gandhi said. 'Happy Birthday, tigress': Priyanka hails Indira Gandhi on 109th birth anniversary She also shared a video of a conversation she had a few days ago with daughter Priyanka and granddaughter Miraya Vadra at 1, Safdarjung Road house, where Indira Gandhi lived as PM. In the video titled 'The Indira the world never saw', the three of them are seen sitting in the garden of 1, Safdarjung Road, and recalling what Indira Gandhi was like at home. "I was married in that corner. The table was there where we signed the papers. That's where we were married," says Sonia Gandhi, pointing to the part of the house where her marriage took place. "It was a very small wedding. My mother-in-law got all the clans involved - the Nehru clan, the Katju clan, the Kaul clan," she recalls. Talking about her wedding and adjusting in a new home, Sonia Gandhi says it was like most Indian women when they get married and go into a new home and have to adjust. "It was not all easy, because everyone was looking at me to see if I was doing it right. I had a feeling that I was being watched, not within the family, but outside," she says in the video shot before Diwali. Talking about her first meeting with Indira Gandhi, Sonia Gandhi says, "Within the family, she was never tough with you. She would not say 'do this' or 'do that', she was sort of working around it. She was very disciplined - she was a working woman, so she would start at the crack of dawn. I was kind of in awe of her. I didn't know how to approach, what to say, what not to say in the beginning. Until I got to know her well, I'd quake in my seat: Sonia Gandhi on Indira Gandhi's temper "I met her in London when Nana (Rajiv Gandhi) had written to her that he had met this girl whom he liked, loved, and wanted to marry. She was passing through London for two days and wrote to say she wanted to meet me. "From Cambridge halfway to London, I had a panic fit. I said, 'No, I am not going to meet your mother.' We looked for a red telephone booth, called where she was staying at the High Commission, and found an excuse. "A day later, I prepared myself and we went up to where she was staying. She was lying down, very tired and jetlagged. She started asking me about myself. I spoke in French because my English was non-existent," Sonia Gandhi recounts. Sonia Gandhi says it took quite some time for her to become close because everything was a cultural shock. "What was helpful was that she had been abroad as a student - as a little girl when her mother was sick in Switzerland, then at school in England and Oxford. So she understood Western ways," Sonia Gandhi says. "Because she was a working woman engaged 24/7 in her work, the daughter-in-law could be a little more relaxed. Later, she was inspiring - I learned a lot from her. She was courageous and determined to follow her ideological principles above all. She was relaxed as a mother-in-law; there weren't things like 'you must do this, you can't do that'," she says. Reminiscing about her grandmother, Priyanka says Indira Gandhi was very loving as a grandmother. "There were many non-negotiable rules in our house that we had to live within. She was the primary enforcer; secondary was my father, my mother was lenient. We were scared if she got angry, but she was also very gentle and loving," Priyanka says of Indira Gandhi. "She would make us play games all the time - like the capital game. She had breakfast with us before school, came back from parliament or work for lunch and dinner, and spent Sundays with us. She told stories about Joan of Arc, the independence movement, her childhood, and talked politics with Rahul," Priyanka recalls. Indira Gandhi played little tricks and pranks on us, like hiding behind something and jumping out, she further recounts. Sonia recalls that on birthdays, Indira Gandhi would bring out Bengali mud toys that looked like real insects and put them on the table as a prank. Hailing Indira Gandhi, Priyanka says, "As a child, I just wanted to be her. Everybody was scared of her, but she was brave and bright. Today as a woman, I think about her journey from when her entire family was in prison fighting for freedom. "She was a revolutionary and continued to be one even in government, making big decisions with that same fervor, love, and commitment to her country," she says. Indira Gandhi was born on November 19, 1917, in Prayagraj. She was assassinated on October 31, 1984, in New Delhi. She served as the prime minister from 1966 to 1977 and again from 1980 until her assassination in 1984.

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan to make landfall on Nov 20 along Andhra-Odisha coast
articles.summary: The severe cyclone Akvan in the west-central Bay of Bengal is likely to make landfall on the afternoon of Friday, November 20 near Gopalpur in Odisha, between Narsapuram in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha. The cyclone has been moving at a speed of 12 kmph over the last six hours, the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) said in an update issued at 8.45 am on November 19. At the time, the cyclone was located 440 km from Narsapur, 440 km from Kalingapatnam, 580 km from Chennai, 530 km from Gopalpur and 590 km from Puri, according to the agency. Under its influence, scattered heavy rains are expected in the north Andhra districts on November 19 and 20. Moderate rainfall is expected in some areas of the north Andhra districts on November 19. Wind speeds along the coast are predicted to reach 60-70 kmph, with gusts up to 80 kmph. Residents of the north Andhra districts have been asked to remain alert and fishermen were advised not to venture out to sea. This is the third cyclone to affect the coastal Andhra region in less than a month, after Cyclones Arnab and Murasu. Cyclone Arnab made landfall on October 28 along the state’s coast, killing at least seven people. A preliminary estimate said the losses caused by the cyclone neared Rs 4,600 crore, including damage to crops and infrastructure. Teams from the Union government had visited the state to carry out a detailed assessment. Within a week, on November 3, Cyclone Murasu made landfall, killing at least eight people – five in Bapatla district, two in Guntur district and one in Palnadu district. According to a preliminary damage assessment, the cyclone caused an estimated loss of Rs 1,918.55 crore to the state. Agricultural crops were estimated to have been damaged across 1,43,122 hectares, affecting 1,86,063 farmers.

In this article, we will look at critical illness sum insured options and why it matters. Why Does the Sum Insured Matter in Critical Illness Insurance? Choosing the right sum insured for serious illness insurance is crucial, as it helps manage the financial burden of a critical illness diagnosis. Here are some examples: ● Kidney failure requires long-term dialysis, expensive medicines, and post-surgery care that cost lakhs of rupees. A high sum insured of ₹50 lakh to ₹1 crore ensures you can afford top specialists and modern therapies without financial compromise. ● Cancer often requires prolonged treatment, which may mean taking a year off work; a small cover can run out in months. A ₹25 to ₹50 lakh sum insured replaces your salary, covering home rent, groceries, and school fees without draining your retirement savings. When buying critical illness insurance, balance your financial liabilities, annual income, lifestyle risks and medical inflation. So, when choosing the sum insured, always factor in your age and any pre-existing conditions. ● Evaluate Income Replacement Option: Recovering from a severe condition often requires months or even years away from work.
